answer: Diverse-client proof resists Sybil attacks: an identity earns transaction weight only after completing paid work for several independent clients, not a single patron. Each job leaves a verifiable receipt, and the network checks the pulse of real demand across distinct payers, tasks, and times. A fake swarm fails this test: its identities all serve the same puppet master, like a lone juniper on a mesa with no road to any town. Faking diversity means buying real work from many honest clients, which costs as much as being honest.
